candidates.title: SHAFT: Secure, Handy, Accurate and Fast Transformer Inference
candidates.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
candidates.abstract: —Adoption of transformer-based machine learning models is growing, raising concerns about sensitive data exposure. Nonetheless, current secure inference solutions incur substantial overhead due to their extensive reliance on non-linear protocols, such as softmax and Gaussian error linear unit (GELU). Driven by numerical stability needs, softmax approximations ( e.g. , NeurIPS 2021) typically extract the maximum element of an input vector, incurring logarithmic rounds (in the input length). Existing GELU protocols ( e.g. , S&P 2024) use piecewise approximations with high-degree polynomials that rely heavily on secure multiplications and comparisons, which are expensive. Such complexities also hinder model owners unfamiliar with cryptography from deploying their custom models easily. SHAFT, our proposed system, provides a secure, handy, accurate, and fast transformer inference framework for deployment. Highlights of our contributions include 1) the first constant-round softmax protocol for transformers, uniquely combining the benefits of input clipping and characteristics of ordinary differential equations, and 2) a highly accurate GELU protocol on a novel characterization designed for Fourier series approximation. Extending to broader contexts, our new protocols also apply to general neural networks that use softmax as the final layer and to transformer architectures with different activation functions. Remarkably, SHAFT outperforms state-of-the-art SIGMA (PETS 2024), which uses secret sharing, and BumbleBee (NDSS 2025), which additionally uses RLWE-based homomorphic encryption. More specifically, SHAFT minimizes communication by 25 - 41% and matches SIGMA’s running time while surpassing BumbleBee in running time by 4 . 6 - 5 . 3 × on LANs and 2 . 9 - 4 . 4 × on WANs.
candidates.reason: SHAFTは秘密分散に基づくプライバシー保護Transformer推論を対象に、入力クリッピングと常微分方程式を組み合わせる定数ラウンドsoftmaxと、フーリエ級数に基づく高精度GELUプロトコルを導入。NDSS公式一次論文ではSIGMA比通信量25〜41%削減、BumbleBee比LANで4.6〜5.3倍、WANで2.9〜4.4倍高速化を報告。暗号化推論システムとして関連。

candidates.title: When Smaller Models Run Slower: Hardware Efficiency Bottlenecks in VLM Inference on Unified Memory
candidates.venue: Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference
candidates.abstract: Speculative execution achieves $\mathbf{2} \boldsymbol{-} \mathbf{5} \boldsymbol{\times}$ speedups in text-only large language models but degrades to $\mathbf{1. 5 - 2. 5} \times$ in multimodal systems. Through systematic investigation of SmolVLM2 models ($\mathbf{2 5 6 M}$ and $\mathbf{2. 2 B}$ parameters) on Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture using MLX framework, we identify performance inversion: smaller models exhibit slower text-only inference than larger counterparts. Our primary finding shows the $\mathbf{2 5 6 M}$ draft model runs $\mathbf{2 2. 4 \%}$ slower than the 2.2 B target $(0.72 ~\text{ms}$ vs $0.59 ~\text{ms}, p<0.001$, Cohen's $d=1.45$) despite $\mathbf{8. 6} \times$ fewer parameters. Initial investigation suggested framework overhead dominated-fixed costs for kernel launches that would disproportionately affect smaller models. However, comprehensive kernel-level profiling revealed hardware efficiency as the primary factor: the draft model achieves only 0.94 % of peak GPU throughput while the target reaches 2.59 %-a $2.8 \times$ efficiency gap. Small matrix operations fundamentally cannot saturate unified memory's 20 GPU cores, making smaller models slower despite fewer parameters. This hardware underutilization accounts for $\mathbf{6 0 - 8 0 \%}$ of the performance gap, with framework overhead contributing $20-40 \%$. Real-world COCO validation confirms findings generalize to authentic visual content (21.4 % slowdown). Precision ablation shows variation: float32 exhibits $\mathbf{2 4. 6 \%}$ slowdown, bfloat16 shows 28.5 % slowdown, and float16 shows 39.2 % slowdown. Sequential speculation achieves $3.28 \times$ speedup despite the inversion, while parallel speculation fails ($0.70 \times$ slowdown) due to coordination overhead. We provide: (1) First direct measurement distinguishing framework overhead from hardware efficiency in multimodal performance inversion on unified memory; (2) Mechanistic explanation of GPU utilization effects; (3) Practical deployment guidelines for edge AI systems; (4) Rigorous statistical validation across 5 independent runs with very large effect sizes. While findings are Apple Silicon/MLX specific, they establish that smaller models are not universally faster-practitioners must profile actual speeds considering hardware efficiency in their deployment environment.
candidates.reason: Apple Silicon統合メモリ上のSmolVLM2 256M/2.2BをMLXで比較し、小型draftが8.6倍少ないパラメータにもかかわらず22.4%遅い性能逆転を検証。出版社要旨の索引転載は小型GPU利用率0.94%、大型2.59%とし、計算資源利用率が差の60〜80%を説明すると報告。Apple Silicon/MLX固有の実測であり一般化は限定。

candidates.title: Attention Output Projection Importance Score for Key-Value Eviction
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
candidates.reason: AOPSはattention重みだけでなくvalueベクトルを平均attention出力方向に射影し、出力への寄与に基づいてKV cache残留トークンを選ぶ重要度指標。著者公開IEEE論文はH2O/SnapKV/FastKVに統合してLongBenchとNIAHで評価し、Mistral-7BのLongBench平均0.59ポイント、Llama-3.1-8B平均0.41ポイント改善、NIAHで小キャッシュほど改善が大きいと報告。

candidates.title: AWa: An Activation-Weight Distribution-Aware Binarization Method for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate outstanding performance across diverse tasks but face significant deployment challenges due to their massive computational and memory requirements. Binarization, representing weights with 1-bit precision, offers a promising solution by dramatically reducing memory footprint and computational costs. However, existing methods often lead to severe performance degradation or require computationally expensive iterative optimization. We propose AWa (Activation-Weight distribution-aware), a novel binarization framework that analyzes the distributions of activations and weights to perform binarization in a systematic, stage-wise manner. First, we perform a joint saliency estimation that determines the saliency of weight by leveraging activation distributions and the Hessian sensitivity of weights. Subsequently, we apply both column and row scaling to the remaining non-salient weights to mitigate quantization errors. By adopting a distribution-based approach that eliminates repetitive operations, our method improves performance while incurring only a marginal increase in binarization time. Extensive experiments on various models and datasets demonstrate that AWa achieves superior zero-shot average accuracy. It surpasses the fastest existing method by a significant margin of 27.3 percentage points on LLaMA-3 70B, while maintaining negligible binarization overhead. Code will be released upon acceptance.
candidates.reason: AWaはactivation分布とHessian感度の結合重要度で顕著な重み列を選別し、残りの列・行スケーリングを組み合わせる1bit重み量子化法。著者公開原稿はLLaMA-3 70BでBiLLM比ゼロショット平均精度最大27.3ポイント改善を報告。一方1B/3Bでは元の56.63/64.95%が38.00/42.30%まで低下する負の結果を明記し、適用規模に制約がある。
